opportunities.title: `distribute()`'s per-beneficiary share math doesn't use the overflow-safe `proportional_share` helper it already uses for the keeper bounty
opportunities.summary: `proportional_share` (lib.rs ~2553-2560) exists specifically to compute `floor(total * basis_points / 10_000)` without ever forming the potentially-overflowing `total * basis_points` intermediate — its own doc comment explains this is safe independently of the workspace's `overflow-checks = true` release setting. `distribute()` uses it for the keeper-bounty calculation (`bounty_amount = proportional_share(total, will.keeper_bounty_bps)`, line ~2586) but its actual beneficiary-payout loop computes the far more common and security-critical share directly as `let portion = remaining * (bp as i128) / 10_000;` (line ~2620), bypassing the safer helper entirely. The one code path in the whole contract whose overflow behaviour matters most — the amount that gets transferred out to real beneficiaries — is the one path that doesn't use the overflow-hardened calculation the codebase already wrote and relies on elsewhere in the same function. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Replace `distribute()`'s `remaining * (bp as i128) / 10_000` beneficiary-payout calculation with the `proportional_share` helper already used for the keeper bounty - [ ] Add a regression/fuzz test with large balances confirmin

opportunities.title: Propose vulnerability identity key and lifecycle schema
opportunities.summary: ### Summary Inspect the committed Anchore JSON fixtures and propose a schema for tracking vulnerabilities over time. Specifically: what combination of fields uniquely identifies "the same vulnerability" across scans? Candidates to evaluate include CVE ID alone, CVE + package name, CVE + package name + version, and CVE + package + image. Write up the tradeoffs, pick a recommendation, and sketch the analytics DB table(s) needed to support first_seen / last_seen / fixed_at / ignored_at / cleared_at fields. **Tech notes:** The Anchore JSON schema is documented at the Anchore project site; worth skimming before diving into fixtures. The goal of this spike is a decision, not code — resist the urge to start implementing. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Written proposal (markdown doc in PR) covering identity key options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation - [ ] Proposed analytics DB schema with column types and rationale - [ ] At least one worked example from the fixtures showing how the identity key behaves across days - [ ] Reviewed and approved by Brandon and/or Matt before next ticket starts ## Bounty: $250 This issue has been selected for our paid contributor program. opportunities.title: `HashedBeneficiary.percentage` is interpreted on a 0-100 scale in `reveal_and_claim` but validated on the contract's 0-10,000 basis-point scale everywhere else
opportunities.summary: `reveal_and_claim` computes the payout as `will.balance * (hb.percentage as i128) / 100` — i.e. it treats `percentage` as a raw 0-100 value (50 means 50%). But `assert_valid_percentages`, which gates `add_hashed_beneficiary`, adds `hb.percentage` directly into the same running total as `Allocation::Percentage`'s basis-point values and compares the sum against `10_000` — the basis-point convention used by every other percentage field in the contract (`Beneficiary.allocation`'s `Percentage(bp)`, `MAX_KEEPER_BOUNTY_BPS`, etc.). An owner who follows the codebase's dominant basis-point convention and passes e.g. `percentage: 5000` intending "50%" would pass validation (5,000 ≤ 10,000, assuming a will with no other percentage beneficiaries per the sibling bug in `add_hashed_beneficiary`) but `reveal_and_claim` would then compute `balance * 5000 / 100` — 50x the intended payout, either reverting the transfer or, depending on balance and other flows, paying out far more than intended. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Standardize `HashedBeneficiary.percentage` on the same basis-point (0-10,000) scale used everywhere else, fixing either `reveal_and_claim`'s payout formula or `assert_valid_percen
